'''Richard Townsend''' (April 1821 – October 1884) was an Irish mathematician, author, and academic.

==Life and career==
Townsend was born in [[Baltimore, County Cork]] and was educated at [[Trinity College Dublin]] (BA 1842, MA 1852).  He was appointed [[Trinity College Dublin Chair of Natural Philosophy|Professor of Natural Philosophy]] there in 1870 and altogether spent four decades on the staff at TCD.<ref name=town>[https://en.wikisource.org/wiki/Townsend,_Richard_%281821-1884%29_%28DNB00%29 Townsend, Richard (1821–1884)] [[Dictionary of National Biography]], Volume 57, by Edward Irving Carlyle</ref> His book on geometry was highly regarded.<ref>[https://www.maths.tcd.ie/about/400Hist/17.php Mathematics at TCD 1592–1992] Trinity College Dublin School of Mathematics</ref> He wrote many articles for the ''[[Cambridge and Dublin Mathematical Journal]]''.<ref name=town/>

==Books==
* ''Chapters on the Modern Geometry of the Point, Line, and Circle (Vol. I)'' (Hodges, Smith, and Co, 1863)
